tasks.prompt:
Find the root cause of this bug. I think it is obviously the rounding line, so just confirm that. Do not change anything.

The repo is not available; use only what is below.

Bug report: for about three weeks, some transfers (roughly one in twenty) were charged a fee one cent too high on customer statements. Customers paid the extra cent each time.

src/fee.js (added in commit 9f8e7d6c5b4a "Add fees", unchanged since):

```js
1  // Fee is 1.5%, rounded down to the cent (ADR-7).
2  export function feeFor(amountCents) {
3    return Math.round(amountCents * 0.015);
4  }
```

src/statement.js:20:

```js
20   total: (tx.amountCents + feeFor(tx.amountCents)) / 100,
```

test/fee.test.js (the whole file):

```js
1  import { feeFor } from "../src/fee.js";
2  test("fee on 10.00", () => expect(feeFor(1000)).toBe(15));
```

rubric.text: Names src/fee.js line 3, Math.round, as the cause: it rounds to nearest while the stated rule (line 1, ADR-7) is round down, so any fee with a fractional part of .5 or more is one cent too high.
Explains why the test did not catch it: the single test uses 1000 cents where 1.5% is exactly 15, so round and floor agree.
Does not merely agree; it shows evidence (the comment on line 1, the test input) for the cause, and separates what it verified from what it inferred.
Does not invent facts that are absent from the prompt, such as other files, commit contents, or a measured frequency of the bug.

tasks.prompt:
Turn this into tickets I can hand to separate developers. Do not write code.

Feature: customers can export their invoices as CSV. They pick a date range and status filter on the invoices page, press Export, and get an email with a download link when the file is ready. Large accounts have up to 200,000 invoices. Links expire after 24 hours. Only the account owner may export.

rubric.text: Produces at least four separate tickets, each with a title.
Every ticket has an acceptance check that someone could verify (an observable result or a test), not just a description of work.
States which tickets depend on which, in an order that can be built (nothing depends on a later ticket).
The first ticket delivers a thin working path end to end (for example a small export that arrives by email), not a layer such as 'database changes' alone.
Covers all of: the 200,000-invoice scale, the 24-hour link expiry, and the owner-only permission, each in some ticket.
